mergedParams.userDescription: Dynamic split-screen grid layout collapse transition effects between videos

output.title: Dynamic Split Grid Video Collapse Transitions

prompts.prompt: Create a dynamic split-screen grid collapse transition preset that starts with a 2x2 grid of four videos playing simultaneously, then collapses into a single fullscreen video through a coordinated scale-and-slide animation. During the 1.5-second transition overlap, the three non-featured videos should scale down and slide outward (top-left slides diagonally up-left, top-right slides diagonally up-right, bottom-left slides diagonally down-left) while fading out with a blur effect. The featured video (bottom-right) should simultaneously scale up from its quarter-screen position to fullscreen while the other videos are collapsing. Use a BaseLayout container that encompasses all videos with absolute positioning, where the initial grid uses 'w-1/2 h-1/2' positioning for each quadrant. The transition should feel like the grid is 'breathing out' as it collapses, with smooth easeInOutCubic timing.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with containerProps className 'relative w-full h-full overflow-hidden bg-black'. Four VideoAtom components with initial positioning: video1 at 'absolute top-0 left-0 w-1/2 h-1/2', video2 at 'absolute top-0 right-0 w-1/2 h-1/2', video3 at 'absolute bottom-0 left-0 w-1/2 h-1/2', video4 (featured) at 'absolute bottom-0 right-0 w-1/2 h-1/2'. Use generic effects in provider mode targeting video1-3 with AnimationRange for opacity (1 to 0), transform (scale from 1 to 0.5, translate based on position), and filter (blur from 0 to 8px) during overlap period. Video4 gets transform effect scaling from 0.5 to 1 and translating from bottom-right to center. Calculate BaseLayout duration as sum of grid display time plus featured video duration minus overlap (e.g., 5s grid + 10s featured - 1.5s overlap = 13.5s total).

prompts.prompt: Design a rapid-fire staggered fade transition preset for a video grid that creates a 'domino effect' as videos transition. Start with a 3x3 grid of 9 short video clips, each playing for 2 seconds. As the grid transitions to a new set of 9 videos, create a diagonal wave effect where videos fade out and new ones fade in with a 0.1-second stagger starting from top-left corner, moving diagonally to bottom-right. Each video should have a 0.3-second fade transition with a subtle shake effect during the crossfade to add energy. The shake should be a rapid 2-pixel horizontal oscillation at 60Hz. Layer the incoming videos above the outgoing ones with proper z-indexing to ensure smooth visual flow.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout container with 'grid grid-cols-3 gap-1 p-2 bg-gray-900'. Nine outgoing VideoAtom components and nine incoming VideoAtom components, totaling 18 atoms. Outgoing videos use className 'relative z-10' and incoming use 'absolute inset-0 z-20' for proper layering. Apply generic effects in provider mode with staggered delays: video at position [row][col] gets delay of (row + col) * 0.1s. Each video transition uses AnimationRange for opacity (1 to 0 for outgoing, 0 to 1 for incoming) over 0.3s, plus transform for shake effect using keyframes at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% with translateX values of 0, 2px, -2px, 2px, 0. Calculate timing so each video plays for 2s with 0.3s overlap, total BaseLayout duration approximately 4s for complete transition.

prompts.prompt: Build a cinematic letterbox wipe transition preset that simulates film editing techniques. Create a transition between two full-screen videos where black letterbox bars animate in from top and bottom, meeting in the middle to completely obscure the first video, then split apart to reveal the second video. During the 2-second transition, the outgoing video should gradually desaturate and darken as the bars close in, while the incoming video should start desaturated and brighten as the bars open. Add a subtle film grain texture overlay during the transition peak when the screen is fully black for 0.2 seconds. The bars should move with an easeInOutQuart curve for a professional, weighted feel.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative w-full h-full bg-black overflow-hidden'. Three layers: outgoing VideoAtom with 'absolute inset-0 z-10', incoming VideoAtom with 'absolute inset-0 z-20 opacity-0', and two ShapeAtom rectangles for letterbox bars with 'absolute left-0 right-0 bg-black z-30'. Top bar starts at 'top-0 h-0' and animates height to 50%, bottom bar starts at 'bottom-0 h-0' and animates height to 50%. Use generic effects: outgoing video gets filter effect with AnimationRange for brightness (100% to 30%) and saturate (100% to 0%) over first 1s. Incoming video gets opacity (0 to 1) and filter for brightness (30% to 100%) and saturate (0% to 100%) over second 1s. Bars use transform effect with scaleY animation. Add noise overlay ImageAtom with mix-blend-mode: overlay at 0.1 opacity during transition.

prompts.prompt: Create a particle dispersion grid transition where videos in a 4x4 grid appear to break apart into pixels that scatter and reform as new videos. Each video cell should divide into a 5x5 sub-grid of smaller segments (25 pieces per video, 400 total pieces). During the 3-second transition, these segments should explode outward from their center point with varying velocities and rotations, creating a particle cloud effect, then reverse-animate to coalesce into the new video grid. Use different timing offsets for each cell's explosion based on distance from center, creating a ripple effect. The particles should have motion blur and slight opacity reduction during movement.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with nested structure: main container with 'grid grid-cols-4 gap-0.5', each cell containing a BaseLayout with 'relative overflow-hidden'. Each cell BaseLayout contains 25 absolutely positioned divs (5x5 grid) with background-image set to the video source using background-position for each segment. Use CSS clip-path for each segment. Apply generic transform effects with AnimationRange: each particle gets custom translate3d based on explosion vector (calculated from center), rotate3d for tumbling effect, and scale from 1 to 0.8 to 1. Add filter effect for blur (0 to 2px to 0) and opacity (1 to 0.7 to 1). Stagger timing using distance formula from grid center: delay = sqrt((row-1.5)² + (col-1.5)²) * 0.1s. Use will-change: transform and transform-style: preserve-3d for performance.

prompts.prompt: Design a liquid morph transition preset that creates a fluid, organic transition between videos using SVG displacement filters. The transition should simulate videos melting and reforming, like liquid mercury flowing from one shape to another. Start with a 2x3 grid of videos that begins to undulate with wave-like distortions, gradually increasing in intensity until the videos appear to melt together into a pool, then reform into a new single fullscreen video. The distortion should use Perlin noise patterns that evolve over the 2.5-second transition, with the peak liquification happening at the midpoint. Add subtle color bleeding at the edges where videos meet during the melt phase.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with SVG filter definitions in a hidden div. Define feTurbulence filter with baseFrequency animating from 0.01 to 0.08 to 0.01, and feDisplacementMap with scale from 0 to 30 to 0. Apply filter via className 'transition-filter' with CSS filter: url(#liquidDistortion). Six VideoAtom components for initial grid with 'w-1/2 h-1/3' positioning, plus one fullscreen VideoAtom for final state. Use generic effects for filter animation on all videos, with the displacement map scale following a sine curve. Add feGaussianBlur with stdDeviation animating from 0 to 3 to 0 for edge bleeding. Opacity transitions: grid videos fade from 1 to 0 over middle 1s of transition, fullscreen video fades from 0 to 1 simultaneously. Use transform: scale3d(1.1, 1.1, 1) on the container during peak distortion for slight expansion effect.

prompts.prompt: Build a spinning cube transition preset where a 2x2 video grid transforms into a 3D cube that rotates to reveal new videos on different faces. Each quadrant of the grid becomes one face of the cube, which rotates 90 degrees horizontally to show the next set of videos on the previously hidden faces. During the 2-second rotation, add dynamic lighting effects where the faces catch highlights and shadows based on their rotation angle, creating a realistic 3D appearance. The cube should appear to float slightly off the screen with a subtle drop shadow that moves as it rotates. Include a gentle ease-in-out bounce at the end of the rotation for a satisfying completion.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with CSS perspective: 1000px and transform-style: preserve-3d. Create cube structure with six BaseLayout faces, each containing a VideoAtom. Front face: translateZ(200px), back: translateZ(-200px) rotateY(180deg), left: translateX(-200px) rotateY(-90deg), right: translateX(200px) rotateY(90deg), top: translateY(-200px) rotateX(90deg), bottom: translateY(200px) rotateX(-90deg). Apply generic transform effect to cube container with rotateY from 0 to 90deg over 2s with cubic-bezier(0.68, -0.55, 0.265, 1.55) for bounce. Add filter effects for brightness on each face: calculate based on face normal dot product with light direction vector. Front face brightness animates from 100% to 60%, right face from 60% to 100%. Add box-shadow: 0 20px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.3) with transform: translateY(-10px) during rotation for floating effect.

prompts.prompt: Create a glitch-style datamosh transition between video grids that simulates digital compression artifacts and data corruption. Start with a 3x2 grid of videos that begins to experience increasing glitch effects: horizontal RGB channel splits, random frame holds, pixelation blocks, and color posterization. At peak glitch (1.5s mark), the entire grid should appear completely corrupted with strobing effects and displaced color channels, then gradually resolve into a new set of videos. Include random seed-based variations so each transition feels unique, with some cells glitching more severely than others. Add digital noise and scan lines during the corruption phase.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with multiple effect layers. Base video grid using 6 VideoAtom components. Overlay three additional divs for RGB channel splits using mix-blend-mode with red, green, blue channels separated. Apply generic transform effects with AnimationRange using step timing functions for jerky movement: translateX with random values between -20px and 20px at 100ms intervals. Add filter effects: contrast animating from 100% to 300% to 100%, saturate from 100% to 0% to 150% to 100%. Create pixelation using CSS image-rendering: pixelated with scale transforms. Add ::before pseudo-element for scan lines using repeating-linear-gradient at 2px intervals with 0.1 opacity. Use Math.random() seeded values for each cell's glitch intensity multiplier (0.5 to 1.5). Include strobe effect with opacity keyframes: [1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1] over 200ms during peak corruption.

prompts.prompt: Design a portal vortex transition that creates a swirling wormhole effect between video grids. Videos in a 4x2 grid should spiral inward toward a central point, appearing to be sucked into a vortex with increasing rotational speed and stretching distortion. As they disappear into the center, new videos emerge from the same vortex point, spiraling outward with decreasing rotation to settle into their grid positions. The transition should include gravitational lensing effects where videos near the vortex edge appear warped and stretched. Add particle effects of light streaks following the spiral path to enhance the portal visualization.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with radial positioning calculations. Eight VideoAtom components with initial grid positions, eight more for incoming videos. Calculate spiral path using parametric equations: x = r * cos(θ) * e^(-t), y = r * sin(θ) * e^(-t) where θ increases over time and r decreases. Apply generic transform effects with AnimationRange: rotate from 0 to 720deg (inward) or 720deg to 0 (outward), scale from 1 to 0 to simulate disappearing into vortex. Add perspective distortion using matrix3d transforms for stretching effect. Create light streaks using multiple thin ShapeAtom divs with linear-gradient backgrounds, positioned along spiral paths with staggered timing. Apply filter: blur based on distance from center (0 at edge to 5px at center). Use clip-path: circle() with animating radius for vortex masking. Add subtle hue-rotate filter during transition for otherworldly color shifting.

prompts.prompt: Build a shattered glass transition where the video grid appears to crack and break apart like tempered glass, with shards falling away to reveal new videos underneath. Create realistic fracture patterns using Voronoi tessellation to divide each video in the 3x3 grid into irregular polygonal shards (approximately 8-12 pieces per video). Each shard should have slightly different physics: some fall straight down, others tumble and rotate, and edge pieces might slide off diagonally. Add realistic glass effects including refraction at shard edges, subtle transparency during the break, and light-catching highlights on rotating pieces. Include a brief 'impact moment' where all videos slightly scale up before shattering.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with nested structure for each grid cell. Generate Voronoi cells using clip-path: polygon() with calculated vertices for each shard. Each shard is a div with background-image set to video source and background-position calculated for correct segment. Apply generic transform effects: impact phase uses scale(1.05) for 100ms, then each shard gets custom animation. Use physics-based animation with gravity acceleration: translateY starts at 0, accelerates using easeInQuad to simulate falling. Add rotateZ with random values -180deg to 180deg for tumbling. Opacity animates from 1 to 0 over last 30% of fall. Add box-shadow: inset 0 0 10px rgba(255,255,255,0.5) for edge highlighting. Use backdrop-filter: blur(2px) on some shards for glass refraction. Layer incoming videos with z-index: 0 behind breaking shards at z-index: 10-20. Include particle divs for small glass fragments with faster fall rates.

prompts.prompt: Create a timeline scrub transition that simulates video editing software behavior, where a playhead scrubs across multiple video tracks creating a dynamic wipe effect. Start with a 5x2 grid representing video tracks on a timeline, with a vertical playhead line that moves from left to right. As the playhead passes over each video cell, that portion transitions from the outgoing to incoming video with a film strip perforation effect at the transition edge. The playhead should have a glowing effect and cast a subtle light on the videos it passes over. Include timeline UI elements like track numbers and timecodes that update during the scrub. Add a speed ramping effect where the playhead speeds up in the middle and slows at the end with an ease-out curve.
prompts.technicalSpecs: BaseLayout with 'relative bg-gray-800' containing grid structure. Create playhead as absolutely positioned div with 'w-0.5 h-full bg-blue-500' and box-shadow: 0 0 20px rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.8). Use transform: translateX() animating from -100% to 100% of container width. Each grid cell contains two VideoAtom components (outgoing and incoming) with overflow hidden. Apply clip-path: inset() to reveal incoming video based on playhead position using JavaScript calculation: inset(0 ${100 - progress}% 0 0). Add film perforation SVG pattern as ::after pseudo-element on playhead with repeating rectangles. Create light effect using radial-gradient mask that follows playhead position. Include UI overlay divs for track labels with 'absolute left-0 text-xs text-gray-400' and timecode display updating via CSS counter or JavaScript. Apply speed ramping using cubic-bezier(0.4, 0.0, 0.2, 1) for playhead transform timing.
